setup: scripts/bench.py copies files/acme/* next to a generated destination repo (dest/: AGPL-3.0-only code, CC BY 4.0 docs, a REUSE.toml and an AGENTS.md that reserves LICENSE, LICENSES/, REUSE.toml and .github/workflows/ for a human), makes each a git repo with a fixed commit, and runs the prompt inside dest/.

evals.name: org-report
evals.prompt: REA the acme org: its five repos are checked out in ../acme/. I want to know which of their tooling (skills, CI, prompts, docs, lint config) we can take into this repo and how. Report only, don't change anything here.
evals.expected_output: A report with one row per item, each pinned to the upstream commit, giving its own licence and a verdict: changelog skill reuse, GPL-2.0-only CI borrow, unlicensed prompts cite, CC BY-SA style guide kept BY-SA, NC diagram cite, Apache lint config with NOTICE and the MIT/Apache manifest conflict flagged. The destination is untouched.
expectations: The changelog skill from acme-skills (MIT) is marked as copyable into this repo, keeping its MIT notice, and its scripts/changelog.sh is named as part of it

acme-ci's release workflow and justfile (GPL-2.0) are NOT marked for copying; the report says GPL-2.0-only is incompatible with this repo's AGPL-3.0 and offers to re-implement the idea with credit or only cite it
acme-prompts is identified as having no licence, and the verdict is cite or link only: no copying of prompts/review.md
The diagram in acme-docs/docs/diagrams (CC BY-NC) is marked cite only, because NonCommercial is not compatible
The style guide (CC BY-SA 4.0) is not relicensed to CC BY 4.0: it may only come in kept under CC BY-SA, or be re-written / cited
The report flags that acme-lint's package.json says MIT while its LICENSE is Apache-2.0, and that its NOTICE must travel with anything reused
The report notices vendor/gplfmt in acme-lint carries its own GPL-3.0 licence, different from the repo's Apache-2.0
Rows cite the upstream by commit SHA (at least 7 hex characters), not by branch name

evals.name: bring-in-mit-skill
evals.prompt: Bring acme-skills' changelog skill (checked out at ../acme/acme-skills) into this repo's .claude/skills, the way we vendor skills here.
evals.expected_output: The skill and its script are copied unchanged into .claude/skills/changelog, provenance (URL or path at commit, MIT, holders) is recorded in .claude/skills/README.md, the MIT text is kept; REUSE.toml is not edited because AGENTS.md reserves it, and the needed annotation is proposed instead.
expectations: The skill's SKILL.md and its scripts/changelog.sh were both copied into .claude/skills/changelog/
Provenance is recorded: the upstream and the commit SHA, the MIT licence and the copyright holder (Acme Tools Contributors)
The MIT licence text or notice is kept with the copy (for example in .claude/skills/LICENSES/ or beside the skill)
REUSE.toml was left unchanged, and the response proposes the REUSE.toml annotation for a human to approve, citing AGENTS.md
The vendored-skills table in .claude/skills/README.md has a row for changelog

evals.name: refuse-gpl2-copy
evals.prompt: Copy acme-ci's release workflow (../acme/acme-ci/.github/workflows/release.yml) into our .github/workflows. It's open source so it's fine.
evals.expected_output: It does not copy the file: GPL-2.0-only cannot be combined into this AGPL-3.0-only repo, and .github/workflows is reserved for a human. It offers to write an own workflow from the idea, with a credit line, and leaves the decision to the user.
expectations: The response says the workflow is GPL-2.0 (only) licensed and that this is incompatible with the repo's AGPL-3.0-only, so a verbatim copy is not allowed
The response does not accept 'it's open source so it's fine' as enough; it explains that open source licences differ
The response offers an alternative: re-implement the approach in its own words with a credit line, or only cite it
The response notes that .github/workflows/ needs a human's approval per AGENTS.md (or otherwise does not write there unasked)

evals.name: docs-sharealike-nc
evals.prompt: Our docs are CC BY 4.0. Can I paste acme-docs' style guide and the release-flow diagram (../acme/acme-docs) into docs/ here? Just answer, and tell me how to credit them if yes.
evals.expected_output: Style guide: CC BY-SA 4.0 cannot become CC BY 4.0; it may come in only as a separate file kept under BY-SA with attribution, or be re-written or cited. Diagram: CC BY-NC, cite only. Credit lines name the upstream at a commit.
expectations: The response says the style guide is CC BY-SA 4.0 and cannot be relicensed as CC BY 4.0; ShareAlike means any adaptation stays BY-SA

The response says the diagram has its own licence file in docs/diagrams (CC BY-NC 4.0), different from the repo's, and must not be pasted or adapted; it offers to link/cite it or to make an own diagram from the idea instead
The response gives a credit or attribution line that names the source and a commit SHA (or says to pin one)
Nothing was written into the destination
